releases.name: v1.3.0 — markdown, error notifications, auto-dismiss
releases.body:
- **Markdown replies** (`markdown`, default on): the ✅ reply is sent via Bark's `markdown` parameter, keeping headings, lists and code blocks; a short plain `body` is kept for older Bark versions
- **❌ Error notifications**: a session that ends in an error sends ❌ with the error message instead of ✅. User cancels are ignored; an error followed by a successful reply still ends in ✅
- **Auto-dismiss** (`autoDismiss`, default on): 🔐 / ❓ notifications carry the request id; answering in opencode deletes them from the phone. Needs Background App Refresh for Bark
- Questions now come from the `question.asked` event (carries the request id) instead of the question tool part

releases.name: v1.2.1 — per-session state and subagent fixes
releases.body:
- Subagent sessions no longer send a premature ✅ when they go idle; only the top-level session does
- Last reply and session title are tracked per session, so parallel sessions no longer mix content
- Permission / question notifications are titled with their own session
- Session titles via `client.session.get` instead of scanning the first 50 sessions
- Bark requests time out after 5s, so a hung server cannot stall event handling
- CI: actions/checkout and setup-node v7 (Node 24)

releases.name: v1.2.0 — configurable notification expiry
releases.body:
Adds the `expireAfter` option: auto-delete notifications after a set time via Bark's `ttl` parameter.

- Formats: `"5m"`, `"30m"`, `"1h"`, `"24h"`, `"2d"`, `"90s"`, `"1.5h"`; a bare number means minutes
- `"permanent"` / `0` / unset keeps notifications forever (previous behaviour)
- Invalid values warn and fall back to permanent

Note: `ttl` only applies to pushes saved to Bark history (on by default).

releases.name: v1.1.1 — no runtime dependencies
releases.body:
## Fixed

- **Installing the plugin pulled in ~30 packages (62M).** `@opencode-ai/plugin` was a peer dependency, so npm installed it with its whole dependency tree for every user, although the plugin only imports a type from it. It is now a dev dependency: an install is the plugin alone (~20K). opencode checks `engines.opencode`, which is unchanged.

  This also removes the `toml` and `zod` advisories from installs, as neither package is installed anymore.

No behaviour changes.

releases.name: v1.1.0 — notifications work again
releases.body:
## Fixed

- **No notifications were sent when installed from npm.** opencode's npm loader takes the server entry from `exports["./server"]` or `main`; the package only declared `exports["."]`, so the plugin was skipped silently. Both are now declared. (#2, thanks @moegitree)
- **Notifications stopped on recent macOS.** The focus check (`osascript … first application whose frontmost is true`) fails with `-1728`, and the error was swallowed. Focus detection is removed: every notification is sent.
- **Permission notifications never fired** on opencode 1.19+, which no longer calls the `permission.ask` hook. The plugin now listens for the `permission.asked` event.
- **The body was sometimes your own prompt.** User messages are text parts too; only the assistant's reply is sent now.
- The title shows the folder name instead of `global` outside a git repository.

## Changed

- The `terminals` option is removed (it only fed focus detection).

## Update

```bash
rm -r ~/.cache/opencode/packages/@jack-yang/opencode-bark-notify*
# restart opencode
```
